summary: As of mid-2026, the LLM landscape is dominated by OpenAI's ChatGPT/GPT-5 family with ~54% of consumer web traffic, though Gemini has surged dramatically to ~28% share while Claude has grown ~855% year-over-year to ~9% share. Enterprise API usage shows a different picture, with Anthropic leading at 40% of enterprise API calls versus OpenAI at 27% and Google at 21%. Open-source models from Meta, DeepSeek, Alibaba, and Mistral have closed the gap significantly on frontier closed models, particularly in coding benchmarks, creating a genuinely competitive multi-model ecosystem.

models.name: GPT-5 / GPT-5.1
models.popularity_notes: ChatGPT holds 53.9% of worldwide AI chatbot web-visit share in May 2026 and OpenAI leads LLM API provider rankings; GPT-5 is available on AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI Service, and Snowflake Cortex, massively amplifying enterprise reach beyond direct API numbers.
strengths: Largest developer mindshare and ecosystem
Strong multi-step reasoning and conversational dialogue
Widest aggregator coverage (Azure, AWS, Snowflake, Vertex)
Real-time interaction capabilities
Extensive plugin and tool ecosystem
models.best_for: General-purpose enterprise deployments, conversational AI, and complex reasoning tasks requiring broad platform availability

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
models.popularity_notes: Gemini grew ~450% year-over-year to 2.9 billion monthly web visits in May 2026, capturing 27.9% of global AI chatbot traffic; natively integrated into Google Workspace, Google Cloud Vertex AI, and available on major aggregators, giving it unmatched enterprise distribution.
strengths: Industry-leading 1M token context window
Deep Google ecosystem integration (Workspace, Search, Cloud)
Strong multimodal capabilities
Available on Google Vertex AI and other aggregators
Fastest-growing major LLM by web traffic
models.best_for: Long-document analysis, multimodal tasks, and enterprises already invested in Google Cloud infrastructure

models.name: Claude Opus 5 / Claude Fable 5.1
models.popularity_notes: Claude reached 952.6 million monthly web visits in May 2026 (up 855% YoY) and Anthropic leads enterprise API usage at 40% share per Menlo Ventures; Claude models are available on AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and IBM watsonx, making enterprise adoption far broader than direct API metrics suggest.
strengths: Leads enterprise API adoption at 40% market share
Top scores on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
Strong safety and reliability for enterprise use
Available on AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, IBM watsonx
Excellent at long-context document tasks and coding
models.best_for: Enterprise API workloads, regulated industries requiring safety guarantees, and complex coding or document analysis tasks

models.name: Llama 4
models.popularity_notes: Llama remains the dominant open-weight model family with tens of millions of HuggingFace downloads; Llama 4 is available through AWS Bedrock, Azure AI, Google Vertex AI, IBM watsonx, and Snowflake Cortex, and is the go-to self-hosted model for enterprises needing on-premise deployment.
strengths: Most widely downloaded open-weight LLM family
Full model weights available for self-hosting
Available across all major cloud aggregators
Strong general reasoning performance
Zero licensing cost for self-deployment
models.best_for: Organizations requiring on-premise or self-hosted deployment, cost-sensitive workloads, and teams needing full model control

models.name: DeepSeek-V3 / DeepSeek-V4-Pro
models.popularity_notes: DeepSeek holds 4.1% of global AI chatbot web traffic and DeepSeek-V4-Pro with its 1.6T-parameter MoE and 1M-token context is ranked the top open-source LLM on multiple 2026 leaderboards; its low development cost and open weights have driven massive adoption on OpenRouter and self-hosted deployments globally.
models.cost_input: $0.27 per 1M tokens (V3); higher for V4-Pro hosted
strengths: Top open-source model on multiple 2026 benchmarks
1.6T parameter MoE architecture highly cost-efficient
Exceptional coding performance matching closed frontier models
Very low API cost relative to performance
Strong reasoning capabilities with open weights
models.best_for: Cost-efficient coding tasks, open-source deployments, and teams needing frontier-level performance without proprietary licensing

models.name: Grok-3 / Grok-4
models.popularity_notes: Grok holds 2.4% of global AI chatbot web-visit share in May 2026 and is deeply integrated into X (Twitter) with hundreds of millions of potential users; its real-time information access and xAI's aggressive model releases have driven rapid developer adoption.
strengths: Real-time information access via X platform integration
Strong performance on math and reasoning benchmarks
Integrated into massive existing social media user base
Rapidly iterating model releases
Competitive benchmark scores against frontier models
models.best_for: Real-time information tasks, social media integration, and applications requiring up-to-the-minute data access

models.name: Qwen3 / Qwen3-235B-A22B
models.popularity_notes: The Qwen family has been adopted by over 90,000 enterprises and Qwen3 is ranked as one of the top open-weight alternatives for self-hosted deployment in 2026; extremely high HuggingFace download counts and dominant adoption across Asia-Pacific enterprise markets.
strengths: Adopted by 90,000+ enterprises globally
Exceptional multilingual capabilities
Strong coding performance with massive parameter scale
Open weights available for self-hosting
Dominant in Asia-Pacific enterprise deployments
models.best_for: Multilingual enterprise deployments, Asia-Pacific markets, and organizations needing strong coding and reasoning in open-weight format

models.name: Mistral Large
models.popularity_notes: Mistral models are available on AWS Bedrock, Azure AI, Google Vertex AI, and IBM watsonx, giving them significant enterprise reach; consistently ranked among top open-weight models for speed and efficiency, with strong adoption on OpenRouter where developers frequently benchmark alternatives.
strengths: Best-in-class inference speed relative to model size
Available across AWS Bedrock, Azure, Google Vertex, IBM watsonx
Strong European data sovereignty compliance
Efficient architecture suitable for lower-cost deployments
Consistently high performance on coding and reasoning benchmarks
models.best_for: Low-latency applications, European enterprises with data residency requirements, and cost-optimized production workloads

models.name: Microsoft Copilot (GPT-5 backend)
models.popularity_notes: Microsoft Copilot holds 1.3% of global AI chatbot web-visit share but reaches hundreds of millions of Microsoft 365 users through deep Office integration; Azure OpenAI Service is the largest enterprise LLM aggregator by revenue, making Copilot's combined enterprise footprint substantially larger than direct usage metrics indicate.
models.cost_input: $30/user/month (M365 Copilot); Azure OpenAI pricing applies for API
models.cost_output: Included in subscription or Azure OpenAI rates
strengths: Native integration into Microsoft 365 (Word, Excel, Teams, Outlook)
Backed by Azure OpenAI with enterprise security and compliance
Reaches hundreds of millions of existing Microsoft users
Strong enterprise IT governance and admin controls
GitHub Copilot variant dominates developer coding assistance
models.best_for: Microsoft 365 enterprise environments, productivity automation, and organizations standardized on Azure infrastructure

models.name: Perplexity AI
models.popularity_notes: Perplexity holds 1.3% of global AI chatbot web-visit share in May 2026 and has carved out a distinct niche as the leading AI-native search engine with strong developer adoption for retrieval-augmented generation use cases; its API allows developers to embed real-time search-grounded LLM responses into applications.
strengths: Real-time web search grounding by default
Strong citation and source attribution
Popular among developers for RAG-style applications
Sonar API provides search-grounded LLM access
Fast response times with current information
models.best_for: Search-augmented applications, real-time research tools, and RAG pipelines requiring up-to-date web-grounded responses
